synopsis: NIED in Japan is named alongside CEREMA, CARISSMA and JARI as a main source of ground truth for weather models [f5056, f16122]. Their weather chambers, including fog chambers, support sensor-model validation, with proving grounds also contributing ground truth [f5119, f15594]. Haider et al. (2023) studied lidar in rain and fog at NIED and CARISSMA, providing a concrete example of facility use [f4731]. However, the booklet did not examine booking lead times, capacity or suitability for heavy off-road machines of the relevant size; these unresolved access questions directly affect model validation before mid-2027 [f16124, f5120].

relations.note: Both identify the same four facilities as main ground truth for weather models.
Both flag unexamined booking, capacity and machine-size suitability.
Specifies fog chambers as sensor-model ground truth at the four named facilities.
Adds sensor-validation scope and proving grounds to the weather ground-truth claim.
Lidar rain-and-fog research demonstrates use of NIED and CARISSMA for sensor studies.
Reliance on chambers and proving grounds explains why access gaps affect validation.
